JsonEditor.Help.Title: Editor help (F1)
JsonEditor.Help.Common:
Shortcuts
  Ctrl+S  Save (JSON plus the related string table / XML)
  Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y  Undo / redo (Ctrl+Shift+Z also redoes)
  Ctrl+H  Edit history: go back to any step since the editor was opened (up to 50 steps)
  Ctrl+N  Add a record
  Ctrl+D  Duplicate the selected records (new Ids, string-table texts copied)
  Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V  Copy / paste records (copies text when a text box has focus)
  Delete  Delete the selected records (asks first; deletes text when a text box has focus)
  Alt+↑ / Alt+↓  Move the selected records up / down (not while searching)
  Ctrl+F  Focus the search box
  Ctrl+B  Batch tools: find/replace in a field, or set / add / subtract / multiply / divide
  Ctrl+Enter  Record the current input as a step now and check for input errors
  Ctrl+R / F5  Reload from disk
  F1  This help

Notes
  Form edits go to memory immediately; Save writes them to disk. The status bar shows whether there are unsaved changes.
  Leaving the editor or reloading with unsaved changes asks: Save, Discard or Cancel.
  The list shows records in file order and supports Ctrl / Shift multi-select.
  Key fields such as Id are applied when you leave the field or press Enter; duplicate Ids are rejected and string-table texts move to the new Id.
  Array fields are comma-separated; unreadable numbers mark the field red and keep the previous value.
  Line breaks in multi-line texts are stored as the game's \n, so a string-table line is never split.
  Saving keeps the game file layout: unchanged records are written back verbatim and unknown fields are preserved.
  If a file fails to load, the reason is shown and saving is disabled so the original is not overwritten with incomplete data.
  The string table reloads automatically when another program changes it; all editors share one string table and each saves only the texts it changed.
JsonEditor.Help.ArmyBuff:
This editor: unit buffs (ArmyBuffSettings.json)
  Unit-level buffs referenced by skills or event effects. Id must be unique, Type selects the game effect, Value / Value2 are effect parameters, Level is the level.
  Debuff / Trigger / Hide / ShowRounds are the debuff, triggered, hidden and show-rounds switches.
  The description is stored in the string table as army_buff_desc_{Id} and follows Id changes and copies.
JsonEditor.Help.Skill:
This editor: skills (SkillSettings.json)
  Id is unique; Level is the level and UpgradeId points to the upgraded skill.
  Type is the skill effect and also the text index (skill_name_{Type} / skill_info_{Type}); all levels of one Type share the texts.
  ActivatesChance is the trigger chance (%); with IfPercent = 1, SkillEffect is a percentage; ArmyBuff is the attached unit buff Id; AurasRange is the aura range.
  CostMedal is the medal cost to upgrade, OpenDefault unlocks by default, NeedStageId / NeedScenarioId are unlock conditions, Score is the AI score.
  A new skill keeps the current skill's Type and writes no new text keys.
JsonEditor.Help.EventBuff:
This editor: event buffs (EventBuffSettings.json)
  Id is the key referenced by EventBuffId1/2 of country events; Type selects the effect (it is not the event Trigger); Value is the effect value.
  Round is the initial duration: -1 usually means permanent, 0 is instant. ArmyBuffs lists attached unit buff Ids.
  The description is event_buff_desc_{Id} in the string table; without it the game falls back to event_buff_desc_{Type} (shown below the description).
JsonEditor.Help.ArmyGroupEvent:
This editor: army group events (ArmyGroupEventSettings.json)
  Chain: EventBuffId1/2 → Id in EventBuffSettings → its Type / Value; Round1/2 is the duration applied by this event. The two slots are independent; slot 2 = 0 means no second effect.
  Id is the unique event record Id; EventId is the army group event set; StageId the stage; CountryId1/2 are the target countries of each buff; TriggerValue / Location are trigger parameters and regions; Chance is the trigger chance (%); PlayerCountry limits the player's country; DisableEvents marks mutually exclusive events as used.
  Title / description are armygroup_event_{Id} / armygroup_event_desc_{Id}.

Trigger
  1 turn; 2 capture the given regions; 3 attack; 4 attack or air raid; 5 chained / delayed event (TriggerValue[0] = previous event Id); 6 defeat a general; 7 nuke / special attack; 8 number of capitals / cities reaches a threshold; 9 chance / turn (depends on the game version); 10 all given regions lost.
JsonEditor.Help.ConquerEvent:
This editor: conquest events (ConquerEventSettings.json)
  Same fields as army group events; ConquerId is the conquest. There is no PlayerCountry / DisableEvents.
  Title / description are conquest_event_{Id} / conquest_event_desc_{Id} in the string table (not the activity intro event_intro_{Id}).
  The ▼ buttons next to EventBuffId and the country lists pick from the event buffs / countries.

Trigger
  1 turn; 2 capture the given regions; 3 attack; 4 attack or air raid; 5 chained / delayed event; 6 defeat a general; 7 nuke / special attack; 8 number of capitals / cities reaches a threshold; 9 chance / turn; 10 all given regions lost.
JsonEditor.Help.Army:
This editor: units (ArmySettings.json + def_armypos.xml + string table)
  The JSON holds unit stats; def_armypos.xml holds the portrait offset and scale (a row is added only when you change a unit's offset); the name is unit_name_{Id}.
  Feature and FeatureLevel go together; Country lists the factions that can use the unit; FormationChance is the formation chance.
  The formation / level simulator applies to the selected units (multi-select) or to all units and can be undone. A new unit uses the current unit as a template.
JsonEditor.Help.Building:
This editor: buildings and facilities (BuildingSettings.json + FacilitySettings.json)
  Two separate tables whose Ids are independent; switch with the radio buttons in the top bar.
  A building's FacilityId points to a facility (use "Jump to facility"). Facility Type: 1 city, 2 factory, 3 research institute, 4 airport, 5 missile.
  Changing a facility Id updates the FacilityId of the buildings that use it. New records use the selected record as a template.
JsonEditor.Help.Country:
This editor: countries (CountrySettings.json + string table)
  Id must be unique; country events, country tech and army group settings may reference it.
  Name is the internal JSON name; the real name shown in the game is country_{Id} in the string table. The two sync buttons copy one into the other.
  Changing the Id also updates the conquest entries and the name; deleting a country also deletes its conquest entries. The right column lists the conquests the country takes part in (read-only).
JsonEditor.Help.CountryTech:
This editor: country tech tree (CountryTechSettings.json)
  Categorys must be 0..4; ResearchLv / Position are the node's row and column; NeedId lists prerequisites (at most 2).
  Lines / Lines2 are the game's orthogonal path points (relative to the node); with Auto lines on, dragging a node recalculates them from NeedId.
  Name / description are shared per Type: countrytech_{Type} / countrytech_desc_{Type}.
  Canvas: drag a node to move it, drag empty space or use the middle button to pan, wheel to zoom, Ctrl+click to multi-select; right-click a node to connect / unlink, right-click empty space to add a node there.
  Ctrl+0 fits the view, PageUp / PageDown switch the category. Deleting a node also removes NeedId references to it.
JsonEditor.Help.General:
This editor: generals (GeneralSettings.json + def_portraitpos.xml)
  Id is unique; EName is the English name and also the key of the head, portrait and portrait position (def_portraitpos.xml); renaming moves the portrait position.
  Abilities and their maximums are edited in pairs; Skills and SkillsMax should agree, skill Ids come from SkillSettings.
  Click the portrait to crop it. The random / specialty templates change the current general and can be undone. Copies get a unique EName.
JsonEditor.Help.ArmyGroup:
This editor: army groups (five linked tables)
  ArmyGroupSettings links to its event through EventId (EventSettings / EventStageSettings / EventCalendarSettings) and to country tech through TechCategoryIds / CloseTechTypes.
  Every army group needs at least one reinforcement or the game crashes; saving is blocked otherwise.
  "Generate army group template" also creates the event, stage, calendar and one reinforcement; copying an army group copies its reinforcements.
  The event intro is event_{EventId}; several army groups can share one event.
